What specific instruments on LRO were crucial in detecting water ice, and how did they contribute to this discovery?

The LRO's Lunar Exploration Neutron Detector (LEND) and the Diviner Lunar Radiometer Experiment were crucial in detecting water ice. LEND measured the flux of neutrons from the lunar surface, which can be attenuated by the presence of hydrogen, indicating water ice. Diviner mapped the thermal properties of the lunar surface, helping to identify cold traps where water ice could be stable. Together, these instruments provided complementary data that supported the discovery of water ice in permanently shadowed craters.
